title: Unused `gleam/option` import added to vacancy_api.gleam
detail: The import is added by this diff, so pre-existing code did not use it; the new code uses `decode.optional_field`, which needs no `option` module. No `option.` reference appears in any vacancy_api.gleam hunk. Gleam compiler will flag an unused-import warning.
recommended_fix: Delete the `import gleam/option` line from client/src/api/vacancy_api.gleam.

title: Submit latch is irreversible if the client-side preflight prevents the submit, permanently suppressing abandonment events
detail: The latch is only cleared by `pageshow` with `event.persisted`. The form has `novalidate` and the documents section documents a client-side preflight in form.js (`// Single source of truth for the client-side preflight: the JS in priv/static/form.js reads these attrs`); if that preflight preventDefaults, the page never unloads, `submitted` stays true, and `onHidden`/`onPagehide` are suppressed for the rest of the pageview — a user who fails preflight then abandons is invisible to the funnel.
recommended_fix: Only latch on an actual unload-bound submit, or reset `setSubmitted(false)` when the submit event's default is prevented / on the next `input` event after a latched submit.

title: Spam render still loads the PostHog snippet despite header comment claiming it "loads no analytics"
evidence:
+//                           ONLY — the spam fake-confirmation page is marked
+//                           "spam-confirmation" and loads no analytics)
...
+        form_view.view_footer(),
+        form_view.view_posthog_snippet(vacancy.short_code, posthog_api_key),
+        ..case with_analytics {
+          True -> [form_view.view_apply_analytics_script()]
+          False -> []
+        }
detail: Only `view_apply_analytics_script()` is gated by `with_analytics`; `view_posthog_snippet` renders unconditionally on spam confirmations, so with consent a bot's $pageview is still captured. The apply_analytics.js header ("loads no analytics") and the form_pages doc ("no analytics script") overstate the guarantee.
recommended_fix: Reword both comments to "loads no funnel analytics" (only apply_analytics.js is withheld), or also withhold the posthog snippet on spam renders if that is the intent.

title: Reminder toast copy inconsistent: possessive apostrophe in singular follow-up but not plural
evidence:
+            0, 1 -> "Follow-up's on its way to one person."
+            0, m ->
+              "Follow-ups on their way to " <> int.to_string(m) <> " people."
detail: Singular uses "Follow-up's" (contraction of 'follow-up is'); plural uses bare "Follow-ups on their way". The adjacent stage-1 strings keep the apostrophe in both numbers ("Reminder's on its way to N people"), so the stage-2 plural reads as a typo in user-facing copy.
recommended_fix: Use "Follow-ups are on their way to " <> int.to_string(m) <> " people." to match the singular's register.

title: Stage-2 2-day gate literal duplicated across three SQL files despite "single home of the rule" framing
evidence:
+      AND last_stage1_at < now() - interval '2 days'
(from mark_followup_reminders_for_vacancy.sql)
+      AND last_stage1_at < now() - interval '2 days'
(from count_awaiting_for_vacancy.sql)
+    AND state.last_stage1_at < now() - interval '2 days'
(from list_awaiting_for_vacancy.sql)
detail: The new view centralises only the rule's inputs (has_unreminded, last_stage1_at, last_stage2_at); the 2-day cadence and the closes_at guard remain mirrored verbatim in the mark, count, and list queries. The spec asked for the gates to be "comment-linked", but the comments link only to the view, not to each other, so a cadence change can silently drift across three files.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit cross-reference comment in each of the three files naming the other two gate copies (or move the cadence into the view as a column) so the coupling is greppable.
